title: Gwacheon Racecourse
description:
Saturday afternoon. When the train pulled into Gyeongmagongwon Station, people poured out.

Inside the Korea Racing Authority building — a smell unique to indoor tracks. Cigarettes, sweat, printed paper.

Middle-aged men lined up at the betting windows. It was {name}'s first time.

No entry fee. That somehow felt dangerous.

choices.text: Just watch for now
choices.result_text:
Watched two races. From the stands, the horses rounding the corners were fast and quiet. More to see than expected.
No betting. That was a choice too.

choices.text: Buy a win ticket (₩5,000)
choices.result_text:
Picked number 7. No reason. Just liked 7.
Result: 4th place. No payout.
₩5,000 gone. Strangely, it didn't sting much.
That was the scary part.

choices.text: Ask a nearby guy how he picks
choices.result_text:
An older man in his 60s unfolded a newspaper.
Recent race records, jockey, weight, weather adaptability.
"Number 3 is strong on this track. But today's weather is a variable."
Ten minutes of explanation. Understood maybe half.

title: The Tip Sheet Guy
description:
At the end of the explanation, the man held out a printed sheet.

Dense tables of numbers. 'Today's Recommended Horses Analysis — ₩5,000.'

"This changes everything. Twenty years of experience, me."

Accuracy unknown. But the confidence was undeniable.

choices.text: Pay ₩5,000 and buy it
choices.result_text:
Followed the sheet and bought Number 3 to win. Number 3 came in 2nd.
Win tickets only pay for 1st. One place off.
Looked for the tip guy. Already gone.

choices.text: Skip it. Trust my own gut
choices.result_text:
Picked Number 11 on instinct. Dead last.
Thought about the tip sheet guy. Hard to say whether not buying was the right call.

title: Number 3 Is a Sure Thing
description:
Back at Gwacheon.

Out front, a man similar to the one before was waving printed sheets.
"Number 3 is a sure thing. Peak condition today."

Last week, a different man had also said Number 3 was a sure thing.

{name} paused.

choices.text: Number 3 to win — ₩10,000
choices.result_text: Took the ticket to the stands.

choices.text: Ignore him, check the records myself
choices.result_text:
Stood in front of the race information board for ten minutes.
Jockey weight, last three race rankings, track suitability.
Looking at the numbers, Number 8 seemed better.
Number 8 came in 3rd. Would've paid on an exacta.

title: Number 3 Result
description:
The gates broke open.

The crowd in the stands rose as one. Someone called out — Three, three.

First corner. Leading. Hope flickered briefly.

Final stretch. Number 3 slowly fell back.

choices.text: Crumple the ticket
choices.result_text:
5th place.

A ₩10,000 bill became a scrap of paper.
Looked for the tip guy. He was already selling a different number to someone else.

Walking down the stairs, {name} checked the time for the next race.
That was the problem.

choices.text: Just laugh. That's what gambling is
choices.result_text:
Worth ₩10,000 for the experience.
Watching horses run was more impressive than expected.
{name} decided to stop there. For today.

title: Exacta Hit
description:
Two races in a row correct.

A perfecta — picking the 1st and 2nd place horses in exact order.

The payout appeared on screen. 18 times the bet.

People around started clapping. {name} stood still, ticket in hand.

choices.text: Collect and leave immediately
choices.result_text:
₩50,000 bet, ₩900,000 back.
Walking to Gyeongmagongwon Station, steps felt light.
That lightness wouldn't last long — that was something to learn later.

choices.text: Ride the momentum for one more race
choices.result_text:
Put in another ₩50,000.
The horses ran. Nothing.

Left with ₩400,000 in hand.
More than before, but the ₩50,000 lost kept coming back.
This is how gambling catches people — learned it firsthand.

title: A Familiar Face
description:
Spotted a familiar face by the betting windows.

A coworker. The quietest person on the team.

Eyes met. Both froze.

Never expected to run into this person here.

choices.text: Smile and say hello first
choices.result_text:
"Oh, you come here too?"
They smiled back. Awkwardly.
"Sometimes."

Neither said more. Each went to a different window.
Monday came and went like nothing had happened.
That was easier for both of them.

choices.text: Pretend not to see them and move away
choices.result_text:
Turned away.
The coworker played along. Probably noticed anyway.

Monday morning they made eye contact.
Both said good morning like always.

Seoul has an unspoken rule — what you see on weekends, you didn't see.

title: Last Train from Gyeongmagongwon
description:
The last race ended.

Handful of losing tickets.

Gyeongmagongwon Station platform. People drifted toward Line 4's last train.

Money spent today: ₩70,000.

On the subway, {name} watched the lights blur past the window. Mind blank.

choices.text: Come back better prepared next week
choices.result_text:
Going to study race records starting tomorrow.
Thinking that, {name} opened the phone.
Installed the Korea Racing Authority app.

Whether this was a beginning or an ending — still unknown.

choices.text: That's it. Today was the last time
choices.result_text:
A ₩70,000 Saturday.
The price of two movies. Not a bad day of watching.
Might come back, might not.

The train moved. Back to Seoul.

title: Every Weekend, Gwacheon
description:
Third weekend without realizing it.

On Line 4 now, {name}'s body automatically stands up at Gyeongmagongwon Station.

A betting pattern has formed. A favorite jockey too.

That part was fine. The problem — the thought of covering this week's losses next week had appeared.

choices.text: Take a month off. This pattern is dangerous
choices.result_text:
Rode past Gyeongmagongwon Station.
The building slid past the window.

Didn't know stopping something could feel this easy.
Because the engine hadn't fully started yet.

{name} read a book that weekend. Strangely light.

choices.text: I can make it back. I actually prepared this week
choices.result_text:
Spent ₩80,000. No recovery.

Counting the total walking down the station stairs.
3-week sum: -₩230,000.

When the number came out, everything went quiet.
That quiet — the worst sign there is. Still didn't know it yet.

title: The Gwacheon Racing Man
description:
A man sitting alone in the corner of the convenience store spoke up.

"You look young — you know horse racing?"

A racing paper densely marked up with highlighter. Late forties. Sipping coffee and jotting down numbers.

"Next Saturday, number 3 is a lock. When the spring rain comes, the inside horses run strong on the Gwacheon track."

You couldn't tell if he was someone who actually made money or just full of bluster.
But there was conviction in the way he talked.

choices.text: "Could you teach me?" — go along next Saturday
choices.result_text:
We agreed to meet in front of Gwacheon Station.
You took a copy of the racing paper. It was packed with numbers and symbols.
You decided to take your first step into the world those numbers meant.

choices.text: Mumble something and slip away
choices.result_text:
You didn't take the racing paper he held out.
What would've happened if you had — you wondered, for a moment.

title: Reading the Racing Paper
description:
The racing man spread out the paper.

Numbers, symbols, horse names, jockey names, track conditions.

"You memorize all this?"

He laughed. "You don't memorize it. You read it."

You still didn't know what the difference was.

choices.text: Learn it seriously — start by memorizing the symbols
choices.result_text:
You spent an hour reading the racing paper.

Trifecta, win, place, quinella, exacta — there were six betting types alone.
Jockey win rates, trainer records, track-specific traits.

It amazed you that there were people who looked at all of this.
You started to get a little of what 'reading it' meant.

choices.text: Just bet on a hunch
choices.result_text:
You picked horse number 7. You liked the name.

It lost.

The man said, "Sometimes the hunch is right. But a hunch is cumulative."
You felt like you understood, and also like you didn't.
